summary: Internal SE enablement focused on messaging for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, competitive positioning, and live demo practice. Team refined objection handling (latency vs cost, security controls), identified slide updates, and agreed on recording a short demo clip for onboarding.
topics: Core messaging: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Demo practice: rollouts, fallbacks, and observability
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Alright team, welcome. It's 3pm so we'll kick off—this is the SE enablement, messaging and demo practice. Roughly an hour.
[00:18] Priya (SE): Hey all. I'll start with a quick run through of the messaging we used last week and then we can practice the demo flow, sound good?
[00:32] Maya (PM): Yep, and I flagged a few competitive points we should tighten up — mainly around cost comparisons and the dedicated offering.
[01:04] Alex: Cool. Imperative we give reps a very quick rubric: when to recommend Hosted, when to go Dedicated, and when Private is required. Priya, run the hosted bullet.
[01:25] Priya: Sure. Hosted: fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, best for early product experiments and small teams. We emphasize streaming, function calling, and curated model catalog. Common objection is "what about PII" — we rebut with short data retention policy and SOC 2 controls. Sometimes customers ask about KMS and encryption at rest — mention we integrate with customer K-M-S (sometimes transcriber hears K-M-S as KMS or 'KMS slash H S M').
[02:03] Alex: Good. Make that line shorter: "Hosted for quick time-to-value; not for regulated workloads unless paired with our Private product."
[02:30] Priya: Gotcha. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, capacity commits, good for sustained high-volume inference. We'll call out autoscaling policies and burst options and the SLA piece.
[02:58] Chris: From sales POV, highlight the economics: per-token delta vs hosted. We need a one-slide calc: typical latency, avg token cost, and when the break-even is.
[03:21] Maya: I'll add that. Also we should pre-bake a slide that shows common workloads and recommended deployment. Eg: embeddings for retrieval -> hosted or dedicated depending on qps; high-throughput chat -> dedicated.
[03:48] Priya: Private: VPC/On-prem for regulated customers. Key asks are audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, and air-gap support. Also customers ask about network topology — they say "how does the control plane talk to my V-P-C?" So we need a clear diagram.
[04:25] Alex: Right — and call out the optional private control plane and what we manage vs what they manage.
[04:50] [crosstalk] Priya: Also a common confusion is caching: KV cache, prefix caching — sometimes they think it stores the whole convo externally.
[05:12] Alex: Emphasize we do automatic prefix/K-V cache for latency gains and it's ephemeral, not long-term storage.
[05:40] [00:06:15] Priya: OK I'll run the demo. We'll start with model selection, then show a canary rollout to a cheaper quantized variant, then forced rollback.
[06:30] [06:45] Priya: (starts demo) I'm in the console — go to model catalog, select a 7B quantized variant, pin to a route. I'm simulating a higher latency threshold, routing policy set to latency-first.
[07:12] Alex: Pause. Say the value prop: "you can route by policy—latency, cost, region, tier—so you get predictable SLOs and automated fallback."
[07:38] Priya: Right. Now simulate traffic spike: switch to canary with 10% traffic on the quantized model. Watch the rollout metrics. Notice token latency goes down slightly, cost per token drops.
[08:05] Chris: Call out the fallback: if the quantized model hits an error, auto-fallback to the full-precision model. That's a big reliability point.
[08:33] Priya: Yep. Triggering a rollback now — demo shows automatic fallback and a canary rollback event in the audit log.
[09:00] [09:30] Alex: That looked good; a few tips: 1) narrate the why — customers want to know why you're switching models, 2) show a concrete cost delta, 3) point to the trace and latency dashboard where they can see token-level breakdown.
[09:58] Priya: Noted. Also sometimes the console names are a bit noisy in the demo video, I'll clean those.
[10:20] Maya: For competitive, a lot of calls compare us to OpenAI and Anthropic on latency and pricing. How are we positioning?
[10:45] Alex: We lean on production economics — that serving and ops matter. If customer cares only about raw model quality, say "we can match or beat on throughput and give you controls for cost/latency tradeoffs."
[11:12] Priya: And versus AWS SageMaker: call out that we provide a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private with built-in fallbacks and easier rollouts. For customers who want deep infra control, SageMaker might work but they'll build more orchestration.
[11:41] Chris: Important: have one-liners for each competitor in the one-pager.
[12:05] [12:30] Priya: Demo continue — now I'll show observability: token-level latency, per-route breakdown, and the rollback event in audit logs.
[13:02] Alex: Quick note: when talking about audit logs, say 'immutable audit trail' and mention retention options. Some customers will ask about retention periods and export to SIEM.
[13:30] Priya: Yes — we support exports and integration with common K-V SIEM tools, but I'll avoid naming too many vendors.
[14:01] Maya: A question we see: "how do you secure customer keys?" We'll be direct: KMS/HSM integrations and RBAC plus SSO/SAML for admin access.
[14:30] Alex: Say it like: "Customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and SSO for admin; we don't have plaintext access to embeddings in Private setups." Might be slightly overstated — caveat as needed.
[15:00] Priya: (mis-says) And we have sock two compliance — meaning Sock-2 — ok that's wrong, correct to SOC 2.
[15:20] Alex: Laughs — yeah, fix that.
[15:40] [15:55] Priya: Ok next part is objection handling practice. I'll play a buyer who says 'latency is too high to use hosted'. Priya (as buyer): "We can't accept p95 of 400ms."
[16:12] Alex (reps): "We can route to a low-latency region, enable KV cache for prefixes, or recommend Dedicated with reserved GPUs for predictable p95. Let's run through cost delta if you commit to Dedicated."
[16:40] Priya: Pretty good. Also include suggestion to run a short benchmark with their workload to show real numbers.
[17:05] Chris: Add to playbook: offer a pilot with metrics collection and a shared benchmark spreadsheet.
[17:30] Maya: About demos — request we record a 5-6 min snippet focusing on rollouts & fallback; this should be in the onboarding pack.
[17:58] Priya: I'll take that. The snippet will be edited to remove console noise and include a voiceover.
[18:20] [18:45] Alex: Quick role play: buyer worried about data residency: they are EU-based and need logs kept in-region. How do we respond?
[19:01] Priya (buyer): "We need logs, audit, and data residency in the EU."
[19:22] Alex: "We offer region pinning for compute and can run private with a control plane placed in customer VPC for data residency. For the hosted option we have EU regions and contractual terms; for sensitive cases we recommend Private."
[19:48] Priya: Good. Include an architecture diagram in the deck.
[20:10] [20:40] Chris: A tricky objection: 'Why not just use OpenAI and call it a day?' We need a crisp 30-second response.
[20:55] Alex: "OpenAI is great for model quality; Redwood differentiates by predictable serving economics, routing policies, and engineered fallbacks—we give you the levers to make inference predictable at scale."
[21:22] Maya: Write that exact phrasing in the one-liner doc.
[21:40] [22:05] Priya: Let's do one more demo run-through, this time I'll intentionally flip a canary to error and we'll show rollback and alerting.
[22:30] [23:05] Priya: (demo) Triggering error... we have an automatic alert created in the console and it posts to the webhook.
[23:42] Alex: Good to show incident hooks — Slack, PagerDuty, and webhooks into their internal ops.
[24:10] [24:45] Priya: One more practical question: how do we talk about quantization? Some customers are scared of quality regression.
[25:00] Alex: We say: "Quantized variants reduce cost and latency; we recommend A/B test them on representative workloads and have automatic fallbacks if quality drops." Offer to run a quality regression with their eval set.
[25:30] Priya: Noted.
[26:00] [26:45] Maya: For the playbook I'll add a checklist: qualification questions, demo script, benchmark checklist, and a competitor card.
[27:10] Alex: Perfect. Action items recap in 5.
[27:30] [27:55] Priya: Quick logistics: could the SEs get the updated slides in the #se-sales slack channel?
[28:10] Chris: Yes, we'll post and pin.
[28:40] [29:05] Alex: Alright, let's do a rapid-fire objection drill. I'll call out objections and Priya you respond. First: 'We need SOC2 and a long retention of logs.'
[29:28] Priya: "We are SOC 2 compliant, and retention can be configured; for long-term retention we can set exports to S3 in your own account."
[29:50] Alex: Good. Next: 'We already have an embeddings cluster on prem.'
[30:10] Priya: "If they're on prem and committed, Private deployment is ideal; we can run the platform behind their network and integrate with their KMS."
[30:35] [31:02] Alex: Time check — about 30 minutes in. Great pace.
[31:30] [32:05] Priya: Final demo note: narrate the policies and show the dashboard; don't dive too deep into infra unless the prospect asks. Keep demos 6 minutes max in initial discovery.
[32:50] Maya: We'll annotate the slide deck with 'demo stops' and 'key messages' for each segment.
[33:10] [33:40] Chris: One more competitive nuance — Anthropic often pitched on safety and alignment; for them emphasize our eval hooks and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[34:05] Alex: Also a short note on migrating models — customers ask how to handle model changes mid-product. We advise pinning routes and gradual rollouts with metric gates.
[34:35] Priya: I'll add that to the script.
[35:00] [35:30] Alex: Recap of action items — Alex will update slides; Priya records demo clip; Maya creates competitive one-pager; Chris updates the playbook.
[36:00] Priya: Any blockers?
[36:20] Maya: None. We might want legal to review the EU residency wording before we ship the deck.
[36:40] Alex: Good call — Chris, can you loop in legal and security?
[36:58] Chris: I'll reach out to legal and security and attach the draft.
[37:15] [37:40] Alex: Ok final notes on delivery: make sure the demo clip has closed captions and a short transcript for sales to reuse.
[38:00] Priya: Will do.
[38:30] [39:05] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after deliverables. Meeting adjourned.
[39:30] [END]
notes: Emphasize production economics and serving controls in all messaging
Record a cleaned 5-6 min demo snippet for onboarding
